name: v1_instagram_profile
title: Instagram - Profile
description:
After recent Instagram changes, fetching creator metadata and posts requires several requests to Instagram, so this endpoint can be slower. If you only need profile details without posts, use [Basic Profile](https://docs.scrapecreators.com/v1/instagram/basic-profile) with the numeric userId for a usually faster lookup. Retrieves comprehensive public Instagram profile information including biography, bio links, follower and following counts, verification status, and profile picture URLs. Private profiles also return all available public profile metadata through the same existing data.user mapper: ID, username, full name, biography and bio links/entities, website/linkshim, standard/HD profile photos, verification, business/professional/category information, public contact fields when Instagram returns them, and counts, without exposing private posts. The response and unchanged status, success, error, message, and billing rules are described below. Also returns recent timeline posts with engagement metrics such as likes, comments, and video view counts, plus a list of related profiles. Useful for account overview, audience analysis, or discovering similar creators. Video play counts are separate from video view counts. Profile-pinned videos may have video_play_count=null when their count is not found in a short recent-Reels scan; available pinned counts are kept and non-pinned videos require numeric plays. Use /v1/instagram/post with an individual post or reel URL for a deeper play-count lookup. Instagram may return media_count as null or return only the current post batch in edge_owner_to_timeline_media.count. Use Profile Post Count when you specifically need the total number of posts. An explicit rendered age gate (for example, You must be 21 years old or over to see this profile. Log in to continue.) returns HTTP 403, success=true, age_restricted=true, error=forbidden, errorStatus=403, and message=Profile is age restricted, without charging credits. This means Instagram identified an existing profile but requires an age-verified login to view it; we do not bypass the gate. It applies to GET, trimmed GET, and POST handle requests. The age_restricted field is omitted when age gating has not been explicitly confirmed; its absence is not proof that the account has no age limit. For GET handle requests, Profile is private means Instagram returned is_private=true. Account doesn't exist means the handle lookup returned no matching account, not confirmed deletion. The historical Profile is restricted placeholder was used for reported content with no public timeline items. Its handler compatibility branch remains, but the current metadata-first pipeline no longer infers restriction from an empty timeline alone; it retains matching metadata as a partial HTTP 200. These placeholders return HTTP 200, success=true, error=not_found, errorStatus=404, and userId=null, and cost one credit. An explicitly rendered generic audience restriction returns HTTP 404 with Profile is restricted and zero credits charged; it does not confirm an age limit. Profile is unavailable on Instagram also returns an uncharged HTTP 404 and does not identify privacy, deletion, or age gating. HTTP 500 with Shoot, IG is blocking us. Try again and it should work. is an uncharged upstream failure, not a confirmed account restriction. Do not label generic login prompts or unavailable responses as age-restricted.

### Profile access response contract

The confirmed-state success flag is intentionally restored to true: success means we determined the profile state, not that the profile exists or its content is publicly retrievable. HTTP 403/404 and zero-credit billing remain unchanged. Actual retrieval failures remain success=false. HTTP status, JSON field names/types, error values, message values, and credit behavior are compatibility-sensitive. We preserve them on existing endpoint versions; incompatible changes require an explicitly versioned contract and advance notice. See the [response-contract changelog](/#response-contract-changelog).

**Confirmed age gate — HTTP 403, zero credits.** For this profile endpoint, branch on errorStatus === 403 && age_restricted === true. The flag means Instagram explicitly rendered an age-verification gate, not a generic login prompt. It is omitted otherwise; omission does not mean false. It does not identify country/region restrictions.

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "credits_remaining": 100,
  "credits_charged": 0,
  "handle": "example_profile",
  "userId": null,
  "age_restricted": true,
  "error": "forbidden",
  "errorStatus": 403,
  "message": "Profile is age restricted"
}
```

**Explicit audience restriction — HTTP 404, zero credits.** This is different from an age gate and from an unavailable profile. There is currently no structured age/region reason field for this case: use HTTP 404, error=not_found, and the exact message below. Do not invent a reason or treat every 404 as a deleted account.

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "credits_remaining": 100,
  "credits_charged": 0,
  "handle": "example_profile",
  "userId": null,
  "error": "not_found",
  "errorStatus": 404,
  "message": "Profile is restricted"
}
```

**Confirmed unavailable page — HTTP 404, zero credits.** Instagram reports the profile as unavailable. This does not establish whether it was deleted, renamed, suspended, or hidden. This response intentionally has no handle, userId, or age_restricted field.

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "credits_remaining": 100,
  "credits_charged": 0,
  "error": "not_found",
  "errorStatus": 404,
  "message": "Profile is unavailable on Instagram"
}
```

**Legacy GET placeholders — HTTP 200, one credit.** These still exist. A JSON errorStatus of 404 is not the HTTP status. HTTP 200 and success=true alone do not prove usable profile data. The three legacy messages are preserved exactly:

**Private profile public metadata.** Private profiles return all available public profile metadata through the existing data.user shape: ID, username, full name, biography, bio links/entities, external website/linkshim, standard/HD profile photos, verification, privacy, business/professional/category information, public contact fields when Instagram returns them, and counts. Full GET and POST handle requests use the complete existing public-profile user mapper; its fields and defaults remain unchanged except that unknown or unusable private follower/following counts are null, while a real 0 is preserved. The count paths remain data.user.edge_followed_by.count (followers) and data.user.edge_follow.count (following).

GET trim=true uses the existing public-profile trim field list, retaining name, biography, bio links/entities, external_url, profile photos, privacy/verification, business/professional flags, category_name, business_address_json, and counts. Full-only fields such as external_url_linkshimmed, business_email, and business_phone_number are omitted from trimmed GET. POST handle requests ignore trim and return the full mapped user, as before.

Full metadata means all mapped profile fields, not raw Instagram internals, private posts, or an age-gate bypass. Public contact information is not guaranteed; unavailable values keep the public mapper's existing defaults. Age-restricted responses are unchanged. Every preexisting top-level field is retained: HTTP 200, userId=null, error=not_found, errorStatus=404, message=Profile is private, and the one-credit charge stay unchanged. POST handle requests keep success=false instead of GET's success=true. The example below shows representative metadata fields, not the exhaustive full mapper output or the trimmed field set. The ID, name, links, photos, handle, and credit balance are synthetic; the counts 560 and 4675 are illustrative and can change.

Historical restricted-result compatibility branch (not the current empty-timeline policy):


These legacy handler branches are retained, but the active metadata-first pipeline no longer emits the heuristic restricted result merely because the timeline is empty; it returns useful matching metadata as a partial HTTP 200 instead. GET trim=true retains the same state-envelope rules. POST handle requests retain a historical difference: these HTTP-200 placeholders have success=false instead of true; they still cost one credit. The POST restricted-placeholder condition is data.user === null, while GET uses userId === null. The explicit 403/404 responses above apply to both methods. A flag-only legacy restricted scraper result is different again: POST can pass through success=true, handle, userId=null, message=Profile is restricted, and isRestricted=true without error/errorStatus. Legacy POST userId requests use a separate compatibility path and are not covered by the handle contract.

**Endpoint scope.** /v1/instagram/user/posts and /v2/instagram/user/posts also return the uncharged 403 forbidden age-gate message, but do not include age_restricted, handle, or userId in that error body. Their explicit restricted-profile 404 says Profile is private, not Profile is restricted. Do not copy this profile endpoint's envelope to /v1/instagram/post or /v1/tiktok/profile; those contracts are separate. Ambiguous upstream failures are not evidence of a missing or restricted account.

name: v2_instagram_user_posts
title: Instagram - Posts
description:
Returns a paginated feed of a user's public Instagram posts, including reels, photos, videos, and carousels. Each item includes media type, shortcode, caption text, like count, comment count, play count, video URLs, image URLs, tagged users, and the published time in `items[].created_at` as an ISO 8601 UTC date. When supplied by Instagram, the media-level `fbid` is also returned. The original Unix timestamp remains available in `items[].taken_at`. Play counts reflect Instagram-only views and exclude cross-posted Facebook views. Supports cursor-based pagination via next_max_id for scrolling through the full timeline.

### Profile access errors

These confirmed handle-resolution states on /v1/instagram/user/posts and /v2/instagram/user/posts return success=true even with HTTP 403/404. A confirmed state is a completed lookup, not a scraper failure. This approved boolean correction does not change status codes, messages, fields, or zero-credit billing. Actual retrieval failures remain success=false. Preserve each endpoint's response contract; see the [response-contract changelog](/#response-contract-changelog).

A confirmed age gate returns HTTP 403 and zero credits. Unlike /v1/instagram/profile, these routes do not include age_restricted, handle, or userId in this error response:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "credits_remaining": 100,
  "credits_charged": 0,
  "error": "forbidden",
  "errorStatus": 403,
  "message": "Profile is age restricted"
}
```

An explicit restricted-profile error returns HTTP 404 and zero credits, with the exact message Profile is private:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "credits_remaining": 100,
  "credits_charged": 0,
  "error": "not_found",
  "errorStatus": 404,
  "message": "Profile is private"
}
```

An explicitly confirmed unavailable profile returns HTTP 404 and zero credits:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "credits_remaining": 100,
  "credits_charged": 0,
  "error": "not_found",
  "errorStatus": 404,
  "message": "Profile is unavailable on Instagram"
}
```

These are the explicit handle-resolution error branches, not a blanket description of every historical 404 fallback. The v2 route also retains legacy success=true HTTP-404 bodies (Posts not found, Account doesn't exist, or Profile is restricted). They differ in fields and legacy behavior from the explicit confirmed-state responses above; success=true alone does not distinguish them. No age-vs-region reason field is exposed. A generic login prompt does not establish age gating, and unavailability does not prove deletion. /v1/instagram/post and /v1/tiktok/profile have separate error contracts.

Play counts can sometimes be inaccurate. Access-response examples distinguish confirmed age gates, restrictions, and unavailable profiles; existing legacy responses are retained.

name: v2_tiktok_video
title: TikTok - Video Info
description: Fetches detailed data for a single TikTok video by URL, including its metadata, engagement stats, and optionally its transcript/captions. Returns `aweme_detail` with `desc` (caption), `statistics` (play_count, digg_count/likes, comment_count, share_count, collect_count), `video` URLs, `author` info, and `music` info; also returns `transcript` in WEBVTT format if `get_transcript=true`. For no-watermark video URLs, use `aweme_detail.video.download_no_watermark_addr.url_list[0]` when it exists. If it is missing and `aweme_detail.video.has_watermark` is false, use `aweme_detail.video.play_addr.url_list[0]` instead. If `has_watermark` is true and `download_no_watermark_addr` is missing, TikTok did not return a no-watermark URL for that video. Also accepts photo/slideshow URLs and returns `image_post_info` when available. Availability is source-specific: a TikTok web page can be blocked in your country while this endpoint still retrieves public metadata, and a post can be missing from the profile feed while this endpoint succeeds. A `404 not_found` means the post could not be retrieved through the endpoint's available public sources; it does not by itself prove global deletion. Keep the last known campaign record and retry later with a relevant `region` rather than marking a post deleted from a single failure. [Examples and troubleshooting](https://docs.scrapecreators.com/tiktok-post-availability). Native captions are opt-in via get_transcript=true and are included in the existing base endpoint price. This detail endpoint does not use AI transcription or an AI fallback; missing captions return no transcript. For AI fallback, use /v1/tiktok/video/transcript. Scrapes a public TikTok video or photo/slideshow. Availability can differ from the web page and profile feed; a not-found response alone does not prove deletion. For no-watermark video URLs, use `download_no_watermark_addr` when present, or `play_addr` when `has_watermark` is false. [Availability guide](https://docs.scrapecreators.com/tiktok-post-availability).

get_transcript.description: Set get_transcript=true for native captions at no extra cost. Missing captions return no transcript; this route has no AI fallback. For AI fallback, use /v1/tiktok/video/transcript.

name: v3_tiktok_profile_videos
title: TikTok - Profile Videos
description: Fetches videos posted by a TikTok user, sortable by latest or most popular — use this to get a creator's video feed or TikToks. Returns `aweme_list`, an array of video objects each containing `aweme_id`, `desc` (caption), `statistics` (play_count, digg_count/likes, comment_count, share_count, collect_count/saves), and `video` (download URLs, duration, cover image). Paginate with `max_cursor` from the previous response, keeping the same `region` and `sort_by` throughout a cursor chain. Known limitation: this feed is not an exhaustive inventory of a creator's public posts. TikTok's web page, single-post lookup, comments, and profile feed use different public sources and request contexts; a post may be retrievable through one and unavailable or missing through another. A missing feed item does not prove deletion, and a returned item does not guarantee browser playback in your country. Try the creator's country with a two-letter `region` code, restarting pagination when changing it, but country selection does not guarantee completeness. Repeated requests for the same page can also return different item sets. For campaign tracking, retain submitted post URLs/IDs and refresh them with `/v2/tiktok/video` rather than relying only on feed discovery. Retry a suspect page within a bounded budget and deduplicate by `aweme_id`; do not merge cursors from separate responses. [Examples and troubleshooting](https://docs.scrapecreators.com/tiktok-post-availability). Scrapes posts from a TikTok profile. TikTok can omit individual posts even after full pagination; region selection does not guarantee complete coverage. [Examples and troubleshooting](https://docs.scrapecreators.com/tiktok-post-availability).
